subject: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch
messages:
From: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch

Hi Jonas —

We've been load-testing the integration and expect a concentrated traffic spike during our Q3 feature rollout (projected 72-hour window). We love Redwood's performance but are worried about short-window overrun costs blowing out our budget.

Two asks: can you provide a short-term top-up path that avoids punitive per-token surcharges, and can the extra consumption be amortized across the next two invoices (rather than billed as a one-time overrun)?

We have a Managed Procurement window next week and need a written proposal to review with finance. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Cross
Head of Integrations — BrightLane

---
Attachments: none

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch

Ethan —

Appreciate the heads up. Short answer: yes, we can offer a contingent bulk-topup with an amortized surcharge option. To make it actionable for your procurement team we usually: 

- Define a temporary uplift band (e.g., +40% throughput for a 72-hour window)
- Cap the effective per-token surcharge inside that band at a negotiated blended rate
- Convert the consumed uplift into a staged true-up split across the next 2 invoices (or applied as a credit against the following quarter)

A few clarifying Qs so we can draft formal terms:
1) Do you need the uplift to be pre-paid (credit) or invoice-then-amortize?
2) Is the spike predictable in UTC window(s or rolling)?
3) Any compliance/approval constraints from procurement/legal we should loop in now?

I'll work with Pricing and Legal on a concrete term sheet. Looping Karthik + Naomi to propose pricing and accounting flows.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, GTM — Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch

Ethan / team —

Thanks for the detail. We've sketched three practical options (summary below) — I'll attach a short term-sheet with the preferred recommendation.

Option A — Provisional Top-up (no prepay):
- Temporary uplift band: +40% baseline for 72 hours
- Blended uplift rate: USD 0.0125 per extra token (capped)
- Billing: uplift consumption invoiced; buyer elects amortization over 2 invoices (equal installments)
- Eligibility: requires PO or written confirmation before start window

Option B — Escrowed Credit (preferred for tight budgets):
- Customer prepays an escrow credit (estimate) at a 10% discount to uplift list rates
- If not fully consumed, remaining credit rolls into next month
- If consumption exceeds escrow, overrun billed at blended uplift rate with amortization

Option C — Contingent Amnesty (one-time concession):
- For strategic pilots we can offer a partial surcharge waiver up to a threshold, with the excess amortized

Recommendation: Option B for BrightLane — gives predictable cashflow for finance and avoids a surprise one-time hit. Attached: "proposed-amnesty-terms.pdf" (term language + sample invoice flow) and a simple billing diagram (billing-workflow-diagram.png).

If procurement prefers invoice-first, we can flip A but will need a nominal administrative surcharge (0.5% of uplift invoice) to cover amortization handling.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call to finalize numbers.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing & Growth — Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: proposed-amnesty-terms.pdf, billing-workflow-diagram.png

From: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearpay.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 07:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch

Karthik / Jonas —

Thanks for the quick options. Procurement liked Option B but wants clarity on two items before we sign off:
1) If we prepay and don't use the full credit, is the residual refundable or auto-applied to next quarter? (BrightLane finance prefers refund, legal prefers carry-forward)
2) Can you confirm the amortization entries: will Redwood produce a single uplift invoice and then two amortization credit notes, or will it be split into two invoices from the outset? Our AP system is rigid — we need the expected invoice artifact.

Also, small ask: can we get a one-line carve-out in the terms that prevents automatic renewal of the escrow credit? We need explicit renewal consent.

If you can send a redlined term-sheet with those clarifications, I can fast-track procurement review.

Best,
Ethan

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch

Ethan —

Good questions. Short answers and next steps below: 

1) Residual credit handling: we can offer either (a) refund within 30 days post-window or (b) carry-forward to the next billing quarter. We'll put both as toggles on the term sheet and leave the checkbox to BrightLane.

2) Invoice artifacts: Redwood will issue a single uplift invoice post-window that records total uplift consumption. If you elect amortization, we will generate two subsequent credit invoices (amortization schedule) that your AP can reconcile. If you need the uplift split into two invoices up-front, we can accommodate but it will add an administrative processing fee of USD 200 per split.

3) Renewal carve-out: confirmed — escrow credits will be explicit opt-in and will not auto-renew unless both parties sign an extension. We'll add the one-line carve-out.

Next steps: Karthik and Naomi will produce a redline-ready term-sheet (we've attached the draft). I'll share a DocuSign link for signature and loop in Legal if the doc requires additional clauses.

Proposed call: Fri 28 May, 9:00am PT — 20 minutes to finalize. Let me know if that works and I'll calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, GTM — Redwood Inference
